name: Riverfront Campground & Canoe Rental
description: Float outfitter and campground with a mile of Niangua frontage just below Bennett Spring, running half-day and full-day trips with shuttle included. Cabins, full-hookup RV sites and primitive riverfront camping.

name: Hidden Valley Outfitters
description: Family-focused outfitter next to Bennett Spring State Park with an RV park of over 100 full-hookup sites, one- and two-bedroom cabins, primitive and electric camping, and a general store called the Trading Post.

name: Niangua River Oasis
description: Full-service canoe outfitter operating on the Niangua since 1977, with four float routes from four to fourteen miles, shuttles for private boats, and primitive camping.
alt_names: NRO Canoe|NRO Canoe Rental and Campground

name: Sand Spring Resort
description: Resort at Bennett Spring combining Niangua float trips and trout fishing with lodge and cabin lodging, RV hookups, an indoor pool, and the Gravel Bar & Grill restaurant.
alt_names: Sand Spring Resort and Canoe LLC

name: Maggard Canoe & Corkery Campground
description: Running Niangua float trips since 1972, including a ten-mile run below Bennett Spring. Shaded riverfront sites with fire rings, 30-amp electric boxes and a showerhouse; no dump station, sewer hookups or cabins.

name: Mountain Creek Family Resort
description: Canoe, kayak and raft rentals with a shuttle, including an 11.5-mile float from Bennett Spring back to the campground. Primitive campsites, cabins and a modern shower house.
alt_names: Mountain Creek River Resort and Canoe Rental

name: Smokey Bottom Resort
description: Raft, canoe and kayak rentals with riverfront camping and RV sites on water and electric hookups, plus a shower house. Formerly Ho-Humm Canoe Rental & Campground, at the same address and phone.
alt_names: Ho-Humm Canoe Rental & Campground|Ho-Humm Canoe Rental

name: Bennett Spring State Park Campground
description: Five campgrounds in the wooded hills of Missouri's busiest trout park, offering basic, electric and sewer/electric/water sites. Campground 1 takes reservations year-round; the rest run late February or mid-April through October.
